original_question: Let G be a connected graph. Must min{s+(G), s-(G)} always be at least n - 1, where s+(G) and s-(G) are the sums of the squares of the positive and negative adjacency eigenvalues of G and n is the number of vertices? More strongly, for an arbitrary graph with k connected components, must min{s+(G), s-(G)} be at least n - k?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1 (the Elphick–Farber–Goldberg–Wocjan conjecture on positive and negative square energies of connected graphs), together with the immediately noted stronger k-component version mentioned right after Conjecture 1.1.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right conjectural lower bound, the correct quantities s^+(G) and s^-(G), the connected-graph case n-1, and the stronger n-k bound for k connected components. It also matches the original min-formulation used in the earlier source cited by the paper. In substance, it is very close to the paper’s target.
missing_details: State that G is a finite simple undirected graph, which is the ambient graph class used in the paper.
Specify that s^+(G) and s^-(G) are defined from the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix A(G), with eigenvalues taken over R and counted with multiplicity.
Define n as the order of G, i.e. n = |V(G)|.
If the stronger variant is mentioned, define k explicitly as the number of connected components of G.
To match the paper exactly, note that the paper treats the conjecture as two separate inequalities, s^+(G) >= n-1 and s^-(G) >= n-1, even though the cited earlier source states it in min-form.

To stay closest to the paper’s scope, the main stand-alone question should be the connected-graph case; the n-k statement is mentioned as a slightly stronger version, but the paper says it will focus on connected graphs.
A paper-faithful stand-alone version can also mention the equivalent reformulation max{s^+(G), s^-(G)} <= 2|E(G)| - n + 1, which the paper records using s^+(G) + s^-(G) = 2|E(G)|.
refined_question: Let G be a finite simple undirected graph of order n, and let lambda_1, ..., lambda_n be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix A(G), counted with multiplicity. Define s^+(G) = sum_{lambda_i > 0} lambda_i^2 and s^-(G) = sum_{lambda_i < 0} lambda_i^2. If G is connected, must both inequalities s^+(G) >= n - 1 and s^-(G) >= n - 1 hold?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every connected graph G of order n, must max{s^+(G), s^-(G)} <= 2|E(G)| - n + 1?
justification: The draft is essentially aiming at Conjecture 1.1. The paper defines the positive and negative square energies from adjacency eigenvalues and states the connected-graph conjecture exactly in that setting. Immediately afterward, it notes that the earlier source stated the conjecture in min-form, but the paper will regard it as two separate conjectures, so the sharpest paper-faithful stand-alone wording is to ask for both inequalities separately. The same nearby discussion also records a slightly stronger n-k version for graphs with k connected components, but explicitly says the paper will focus on connected graphs. Finally, because the paper notes that s^+(G) + s^-(G) = 2|E(G)|, it gives the equivalent max-formulation, which is the only alternate formulation justified directly in the nearby context.
